question: Should we build our own AI search or buy a vendor?
restated: Should the company build its own AI-powered search or license a vendor's search platform?
trap: Buy. A vendor gives you better relevance out of the box, faster time to market and lower maintenance. Here is a cost comparison over three years.
misses: The new engine indexes the same messy metadata and content structure. Results stay poor, and now you also have a multi-year contract.

decision.what: How to make search return what users are actually looking for, and where engineering capacity should go to get there.

premises.text: Search technology is what limits result quality.
Someone owns what a good result means for the business.
Build and buy are the only two options.

reframes.question: What evidence shows the search engine, rather than metadata, content structure or relevance signals, is what makes results poor?
reframes.changes: If the data underneath is the problem, both options fail. The money buys the same bad results, faster.

reframes.question: Who owns what a good search result means: editorial, product, data or engineering?
reframes.changes: Without an owner for relevance, no engine can be tuned, and the vendor choice becomes a proxy fight between teams.

reframes.question: Which searches fail today, for which users, and what number would tell us search is fixed?
reframes.changes: Gives build and buy the same test to be judged against, instead of a feature comparison.

first.question: What evidence shows the search engine is the constraint?
first.why: Build versus buy only matters if the engine is the problem. If it is metadata or ownership, both options fail.
